children: New Zealand stocks rose 24 points, or 0.2%, to 13,735 on Thursday, moving up from their lowest level since July 31, touched a day earlier, mainly buoyed by consumer discretionary, healthcare, and real estate.
However, traders were cautious ahead of the release of US inflation data later today for clues on the Fed's monetary policy decision next week.
Caution also built ahead of the release of New Zealand's GDP for Q2 and a slew of data from China, New Zealand's top trading partner, due next week.
A downbeat session on Wall Street overnight also capped the gain, amid a surge in Treasury yields and rising oil prices.

On the data front, New Zealand’s manufacturing sector expanded at a slower pace in August. Among earlier gainers were Hallenstein Glasson (1.6%), Ebos Group (1.1%), Chorus (0.7%), F&C Investment (0.6%), and ANZ Group (0.2%).
For the week, the index is heading for a 1.5% fall, after rising in the previous week.

title: NZX 50 Gains but Set for Weekly Decline
